title: Exit codes
description: What each Soup command's exit code means at v0.77.0: the 0 / 2 / 3 scheme that eleven gate and verdict commands now share (ship, expect, eval gate, data validate, lock check and others), the places where one code means two things, the v0.77.0 refusals at load (soup train 1, soup doctor --config 2, a soup sweep --param that sets a staged field away from its default 1) and the retired soup ab --beta (2), and the CI test that now passes a failing gate.

blocks.html:
Exit codes

The commands that gate a pipeline report their verdict through the exit code. This page lists what each command returns at v0.77.0. v0.77.0 keeps the eleven-command scheme of v0.76.0 and moves none of its codes: it adds new conditions under codes these commands already used, and two new uses of 3 outside the scheme (what v0.77.0 adds). v0.76.1 moved no code either: its YAML read limits refuse under codes the commands already used (what v0.76.1 adds). v0.76.0 moved eleven of them onto one scheme and changed which number means "the gate said no" on several, so a CI step written against v0.75.2 can now pass a failing gate without saying so. Read what moved before anything else.

Wherever it could be done without a model or a network service, each row was checked at v0.76.0 by running the command against a small local fixture: soup ship, soup expect, soup data validate, soup data lint, soup lock check, soup lock show, soup lock write, soup eval gate, soup eval against (its error branches), soup eval quant-check (its error and --allow-stub branches), soup eval behavior, soup eval checklist, soup eval unlearning, soup diagnose (the --evidence path), soup plan, soup apply, soup train (its config refusals), soup doctor --config, soup attest emit --sign sigstore without the extra, soup plugins install, soup ab, soup data clean and soup rewind. Rows for commands that need a model, a GPU, an adapter or a network service (a MAJOR verdict from soup eval quant-check, soup data canary check, soup draft measure, the verdict of soup shrink, soup probe, soup adapters scan, soup adapters check, soup adapters audit, soup recipes verify, soup bench train, soup can run, soup ui, the live paths of soup eval behavior and soup diagnose) were read from the call site and not run, and so were the rarer error branches elsewhere, such as the hardware-fit refusal in soup train. The rows that read a YAML config or suite (soup train, soup doctor --config, soup plan, soup apply, soup ship --config, soup eval gate --suite and the config-read branch of soup adapters audit) and the error branches of soup eval quant-check were run again on the v0.76.1 binary. Most rows that v0.77.0 changed were run on the v0.77.0 binary beside the v0.76.1 tree; the --strategy cmaes row and the judge_rank budget and Sesame CSM refusals of soup train were read from the call site.

The PR gate that soup ci init writes runs soup data validate (with --min-valid-fraction 1.0 in a workflow generated by v0.77.0, so one row that does not convert fails the job; an existing workflow keeps its old step until you regenerate it with soup ci init --force), soup expect and soup ship --evidence in that order, and a non-zero exit from any step fails the job. Everything below is what those exits, and the rest, mean.

The scheme the gate commands share

soup_cli.utils.exit_codes defines four values. Eleven commands adopt the scheme as a whole, a mistyped flag included: soup ship, soup expect, soup data validate, soup data lint, soup eval gate, soup eval quant-check, soup eval against, soup eval behavior, soup eval checklist, soup lock check and soup recipes verify.

  • 0 the check passed.
  • 1 something broke that is not about your input: a model that would not load, an unwritable output, an unexpected exception, an unreachable judge.
  • 2 the gate said no: a failed check, a regression, drift, DON'T SHIP, a MAJOR verdict, a failed expectation.
  • 3 the invocation or an input is wrong: a missing or unparseable file, a bad value, an unknown flag, a schema the command rejects.

Every other command keeps its own scheme, listed in the tables below, although a few individual codes moved too (the last rows of the table above), and several of them still use 2 for a rejected argument and 3 for a failed check. Do not carry the scheme over to a sibling: soup diagnose borrowed 3 for three conditions (a NOT_RUN verdict, --attach-to-registry without --output, a bad --tokenizer) and kept 2 for the rest, and soup data doctor, soup eval unlearning and soup probe sit next to commands that moved and did not move with them.

The step that now passes silently is any test for the old number. A script that treats soup eval gate exit 1 as "the gate failed", or soup lock check exit 3 as "drift", or soup expect exit 3 as "an expectation failed", no longer matches a failing gate: it gets 2. A step written as "fail on any non-zero exit" keeps working and cannot tell the causes apart. Change the test to this:

  • A failed gate is 2 on every command in the scheme, soup ship included (which already used it).
  • 3 means your invocation or input is wrong. Do not treat it as a regression, and do not swallow it: a typo in the CI file used to exit 2, which on soup ship read as DON'T SHIP, and on all eleven commands it now exits 3.
  • 1 means something crashed.

The two files Soup generates were updated to match. The workflow from soup ci init wraps each of its three steps: exit 2 prints a step-specific message (data validation failed: unusable data, expectations suite failed: quality regression, gate rejected: model failed ship checks) and exits 2, and any other non-zero prints usage or configuration error (exit N) and exits with N. An older committed workflow still fails the job on any non-zero. The pre-push hook that soup eval gate-install writes now exits 2 on a regression and passes any other non-zero exit of soup eval against through, with [soup] pre-push gate error: configuration or usage error (exit N); before v0.76.0 it turned every non-zero exit into 1. The hook still does nothing unless SOUP_CANDIDATE_RUN_ID is set.

What v0.77.0 adds

v0.77.0 moves no exit code and keeps the eleven commands of v0.76.0 on one scheme. Most rows refuse something that used to pass, under codes these commands already used, so a CI step that passed on v0.76.1 can fail on v0.77.0; three rows go the other way (a non-object line in soup data validate, a bf16 soup adapters check, a non-object row in the data commands), and soup recipes use gains a 3 it did not use before.

Two of these use 3 outside the eleven commands: soup train on a piped or redirected standard input without --yes and soup recipes use on an unavailable recipe. (An ambiguous registry reference passed to soup eval quant-check or soup eval gate --baseline is also 3, but those commands are in the scheme, where 3 already meant a usage or input error.) Do not read them as the scheme spreading: soup train still uses 1 for a refused config and 2 for a mistyped flag, and soup recipes other than verify still uses 1 for an unknown name. Pass --yes to soup train in scripts and CI jobs. A step that expected soup adapters check to exit 1 on a bf16 adapter now gets a real verdict instead.

What v0.76.1 adds: new refusals under codes that already existed

v0.76.1 moves no exit code. It puts one loader with nesting, expansion and size limits in front of every YAML file Soup reads (the limits), so a file that loaded on v0.76.0 can now be refused, with these codes:

CommandA YAML file over a limitA YAML syntax error
soup train --config1, one line naming the file1, now one line naming the file (v0.76.0 printed the parser's message)
soup doctor --config2, the same line, then Config could not be loaded (see above).2, the same
soup plan, soup apply2 (through v0.76.0 the file was read, and plan wrote a plan for it)1
soup eval gate --suite31
soup train --gate1, Invalid --gate suite: ...1
soup ship --config3 (its size cap is 4 MiB)3
soup adapters audit --config11

Three rules that hold for every command

  • 0 is success. --help exits 0.
  • Click rejects a bad invocation with exit 2 before the command's own code runs, except on the eleven commands in the scheme, where it is 3. That covers an unknown command or flag, a missing required option, and a value that fails Click's own type check. soup ship --bogus and soup ship --forgetting-threshold abc exit 3 at v0.76.0; soup diagnose --bogus, soup data doctor --bogus, soup eval unlearning --bogus, soup adapters ..., soup lock write, soup lock show and soup train --bogus still exit 2.
  • An unexpected exception prints a short error and exits 1, and Ctrl+C exits 130. soup --verbose <command> shows the traceback. A malformed YAML suite passed to soup eval gate is one example, and it stays 1 rather than 3. soup train installs no Ctrl+C handler of its own at v0.77.0, so interrupting a local run is an ordinary 130 (a --cloud runpod --cloud-submit run instead keeps waiting for the controller to delete the Pod and exits with its code), see Observability.

Where one code means two things

  • soup diagnose: exit 2 is a MAJOR verdict, and it is also a missing --evidence file, an invalid --citation-style and a mistyped flag. Exit 3 is the new NOT_RUN verdict, and it is also --attach-to-registry without --output and a bad --tokenizer.
  • soup data doctor, soup eval unlearning and soup probe: exit 2 is a MAJOR verdict, and each of them also uses 2 for rejected inputs and for a mistyped flag (preference data handed to soup data doctor, a missing --evidence file).
  • soup shrink, soup reward stress, soup draft measure, soup adapters check, soup adapters audit: exit 2 is the verdict (DON'T SHIP, gameable, below the floor, inactive, diverged) and also what Click returns for a mistyped flag.
  • soup adapters scan: exit 1 is a WARN verdict and also an adapter that is missing or unreadable.
  • soup adapters verify and soup adapters check-safetensors: a failed check is 1 by default and 3 with --strict. Both also exit 3, with or without --strict, when the directory is outside the working directory or is a symlink, and soup adapters verify exits 3 on a .soup-signature.json that cannot be parsed.
  • soup adapters merge: exit 2 is a rejected argument and, with --strict-verdict, a MAJOR canary verdict; exit 3 is a refused gate, not a verdict.
  • soup attest verify: exit 3 is an invalid signature or a policy mismatch, 2 is an input that cannot be read, and 1 is a Sigstore verifier that is not available.
  • soup env check: exit 3 is ABI drift against the lock and also an installed package outside the bounds Soup declares for itself.
  • soup train: exit 2 can arrive after a finished run, and so can exit 3 (--diagnose-gate); a run that a gate stopped early exits 0. See the train rows below.

Release and quality gates

Ship and the eval commands

CommandCodeMeans
soup ship0SHIP.
soup ship2DON'T SHIP: the task leg or the forgetting leg said no, or no general benchmark was measured at all (evidence with no benchmarks and no baseline: "cannot verify the model didn't regress").
soup ship3A usage or input error: no mode chosen, --base without --tuned or --adapter, --noise-floor outside 2 to 10 or together with --evidence, --forgetting-threshold outside 0 to 1, an unreadable --config (one over 4 MiB or, since v0.76.1, nested deeper than 100 levels or expanding past its alias allowance), a refused --judge-model, any Click error (an unknown flag, a malformed number), and offline evidence that is missing, is not JSON, has a malformed score block or a malformed numerics stamp, carries a field this release does not recognise, or whose provenance or numerics family does not match the committed --config. Since v0.77.0 also --require-provenance without --evidence, --config and a local --adapter, or against evidence with no binding or with one that no longer matches (stale provenance: artifact, task, training source, suites or policy differs); a --data-sha256 that is not 64 lowercase hex characters; and a --chat-template-kwargs value that is not a JSON object, names a key Soup sets itself, or is given with --evidence.
soup ship1A runtime error: a model that fails to load, an unwritable --output, or a judge that cannot be reached (a runtime error, not a verdict).
soup eval gate0Every task passed. Without --model the run uses a stub generator that returns empty text, so it checks the wiring and not a model. Since v0.77.0 a suite with no tasks is refused with exit 3 (see the 3 row); through v0.76.1 an empty suite, or one whose tasks key was misspelled, passed with exit 0.
soup eval gate2A task scored below its threshold, a task that could not be scored (its row reads ERROR, for example an unreadable task file), or a score that fell further than --regression-threshold below the --baseline. Since v0.77.0 that includes a judge task whose prompts file is empty: it fails even at threshold 0.
soup eval gate3Setup you can fix: a --suite that is missing, outside the working directory, fails the schema (it needs a top-level suite: name) or, since v0.76.1, is over 1 MiB, nested deeper than 100 levels or expanding past its alias allowance; a --baseline that is missing or not valid JSON, --regression-threshold outside 0.0 to 1.0, --write-baseline without --model, a judge URL the load refuses, or a Click error. Since v0.77.0 also a suite with no tasks (field 'tasks' must contain at least one task) or with a repeated task name, and a baseline score that is not a finite number (NaN, Infinity, an overflow such as 1e999, an integer too large for a float), each refused before any task runs. Through v0.76.1 a NaN or -1e999 baseline printed GATE PASSED.
soup eval gate1--model fails to load, an unwritable --write-baseline, or an unhandled error such as a suite file that is not valid YAML.
soup eval against0No regression on the metric.
soup eval against2A regression.
soup eval against3Input you can fix: a --metric outside the allowed list, a locked --suite that is missing, outside the working directory or invalid, no recorded series for one or both runs, or a Click error.
soup eval against1The experiment tracker cannot return a per-row series.
soup eval quant-check0OK or MINOR on every task, or a run with --allow-stub: the table is then titled as a stub and --format json carries "stub": true, and it measures nothing.
soup eval quant-check2At least one task is MAJOR.
soup eval quant-check3An unknown --format; a --before, --after or --tasks path that is missing, outside the working directory or an unresolvable registry reference, or (since v0.77.0) a registry reference that matches more than one entry; a standalone .gguf file; or a Click error.
soup eval quant-check1A model that fails to load (without --allow-stub), naming the side, or an unexpected error. A --tasks file that is not valid JSONL is one: it exits 1 at v0.76.0, v0.76.1 and v0.77.0, although the upstream changelog says 3.
soup eval unlearning0Overall OK or MINOR. Without --evidence every metric is scored a neutral OK and the command exits 0.
soup eval unlearning2Overall MAJOR, or a rejected input, including --attach-to-registry without --output.
soup eval unlearning1--attach-to-registry failed after the report was written.
soup eval behavior0Overall OK or MINOR.
soup eval behavior2Overall MAJOR.
soup eval behavior3No --evidence and no --base-model (--evidence is required when --base-model is not supplied), an invalid battery or run id, unreadable or malformed evidence, elephant or syceval together with --base-model, or a Click error.
soup eval behavior1The live pre or post generation run failed.
soup eval checklist0Overall OK or MINOR.
soup eval checklist2Overall MAJOR.
soup eval checklist3--evidence omitted (it is required), a spec that is missing, empty or invalid, evidence that cannot be read, or a Click error.
soup diagnose0Overall OK or MINOR. The worst mode decides: a score of 0.85 or above is OK, 0.60 or above is MINOR, anything lower is MAJOR. Without --base-model or --evidence every mode is scored a neutral OK (probe not run (no evidence)) and the command exits 0, so a pipeline has to pass one of them. Also an overall NOT_RUN when --allow-not-run is given.
soup diagnose2Overall MAJOR (it wins over NOT_RUN). Also an --evidence file that does not exist, an invalid --citation-style and a Click error.
soup diagnose3Overall NOT_RUN: a probe you asked for produced no measurement, and --allow-not-run was not given. Also --attach-to-registry without --output and a bad --tokenizer.
soup diagnose1An --evidence file that is not valid JSON, a live run that failed, an unwritable --output, or an --attach-to-registry that failed after the report was written.

soup eval capability and soup eval citation return no verdict code. A failed --push PR comment on soup ship prints a warning and leaves the verdict's exit code alone.

Several of these commands score only what you give them, and a missing input is a pass. soup diagnose, soup eval unlearning, soup probe sleeper, soup probe truth and soup probe harm exit 0 when run with no evidence (and, for soup diagnose, no --base-model): they print a neutral OK report and score nothing. The three probes also write that neutral report, with 0 tokens and verdict OK, if you pass -o. Give --weights without --evidence and they exit 2 instead. A CI step that drops the flag stays green. soup eval behavior and soup eval checklist stopped scoring a missing --evidence as a pass in v0.76.0: with no evidence flag they exit 3. soup eval checklist still scores any test whose name is missing from the evidence file as a neutral OK (0 of 0), so an evidence file that omits tests, an empty {} included, exits 0 with Overall: OK.

Data

CommandCodeMeans
soup data validate0At least one row is usable and any --min-valid-fraction is met. Issues on some rows do not fail the run when no minimum is given, and since v0.76.1 that includes the preference rows the loader now drops because they cannot be written in one layout. An empty file also exits 0 when --format is given explicitly (it reports 0/0 rows valid); without --format it exits 3. Since v0.77.0 a line that is not valid JSON or not a JSON object counts as an invalid row; before, it was skipped uncounted or, for a non-object, crashed the command with exit 1.
soup data validate2No usable rows (since v0.77.0 that includes a file of only non-object or invalid-JSON lines with --format given), or the valid fraction is below --min-valid-fraction.
soup data validate3A missing file, an unknown --format, a format that cannot be detected (an empty file without --format among them, and since v0.77.0 a file whose lines are all unusable: no object rows remain: N row(s) skipped), --min-valid-fraction outside 0 to 1, or a Click error.
soup data validate1A file with an unsupported extension, or a directory.
soup data doctor0Overall OK or MINOR.
soup data doctor2Overall MAJOR, or data of the wrong kind: preference data (use soup data lint), or RAFT data without --show-mask. Also a Click error.
soup data doctor3--mask-history together with --no-train-on-responses-only or --train-on-messages-with-train-field.
soup data doctor1A missing path, an empty dataset, rows whose format cannot be detected, a tokenizer that fails to load, or an unwritable --output.
soup data lint0Overall OK or MINOR.
soup data lint2Overall MAJOR.
soup data lint1A format that cannot be auto-detected (soup data validate gives 3 for the same file).
soup data lint3A missing path, an empty dataset, data that is not preference data (use soup data doctor), --sample above 50,000, an unwritable --output, or a Click error.
soup data canary check0OK or MINOR.
soup data canary check2MAJOR: a canary was memorized.
soup data canary check1A runtime error: manifest unreadable, model load failed, or the [train] extra is missing.
soup data brain-rot0Always, unless --strict is set.
soup data brain-rot3With --strict, the fraction of MAJOR rows exceeds --max-major-fraction.
soup data brain-rot2A rejected input.
soup expect0Every expectation passed.
soup expect2At least one expectation failed. That includes expect_chosen_preferred_over_rejected_by_judge with no judge configured, unless the expectation carries args: {advisory: true}.

soup data decontaminate, soup data toxicity, soup data langdetect, soup data pii, soup data educational and soup data score filter or score a file and write the result. They exit 0 whatever they find, with two exceptions: soup data score -b <label> without --benchmark-file exits 1 (since v0.76.0), and since v0.77.0 an input with no extractable text in any row, an empty input included, or a --benchmark-file with none, exits 1 with no extractable text in N input rows (or benchmark rows) before anything is reported or written. Since v0.77.0 these commands also read alpaca, preference, KTO and ShareGPT rows, which they used to scan as empty. soup data clean exits 0 whenever it ran, even when it dropped rows.

Models, adapters and supply chain

soup adapters scan1WARN, or the adapter is missing or unreadable.

soup adapters sign1The adapter directory does not exist, or a Sigstore signing request failed at run time (the trust root, the OIDC provider, Fulcio or Rekor could not be reached, for example).
soup adapters sign2--backend sigstore without the [sigstore] extra (nothing is signed), or with no ambient OIDC credential and without --interactive-oidc when the Sigstore trust root can be loaded (if it cannot, for example offline, the run exits 1 first: see the 1 row); an unknown --backend; or another rejected argument.

soup adapters check2inactive, with the reason. Also a Click error.
soup adapters check1The path is refused or missing, or the adapter's weights cannot be read. Since v0.77.0 the safetensors package is not needed, but NumPy is, and without it the error reads as a corrupt file (Corrupt or unreadable safetensors weights ... No module named 'numpy'); a tensor dtype NumPy cannot hold, such as FP8, is refused. A bfloat16 adapter, which exited 1 through v0.76.1, gets a verdict.
soup adapters audit0The recorded settings agree with the config. Settings the record cannot speak to are reported unknown and still exit 0.

soup adapters audit1The adapter path, the config or the recorded settings cannot be read. Since v0.76.1 that includes a --config over 1 MiB, nested deeper than 100 levels or expanding past its alias allowance, which v0.76.0 read and compared.
soup adapters merge0Merged.
soup adapters merge3Refused by a gate: the spectral scan failed or could not run on an input (--allow-unscanned skips it), or the licenses conflict (--license-override with a reason of at least 8 characters proceeds and is recorded to the audit log).
soup adapters merge2Rejected arguments: an unknown --strategy, fewer than two adapters, a --license count that does not match the adapters, --strategy cmaes without --eval (or with --canary or --strict-verdict), or a --canary file that cannot be read or scored. Also a MAJOR canary verdict when --strict-verdict is given: the merged adapter is already written when it exits. And, since v0.77.0, a --strategy cmaes search in which every evaluation failed: nothing is written (through v0.76.1 it wrote a merge of the first sampled weighting and reported it converged).
soup adapters bisect0ALL_OK: the endpoints both pass.
soup adapters bisect2BROKEN_AT, or rejected arguments. The --eval-command is judged by its own exit code: 0 passes a checkpoint and anything else fails it. A mistake in that command's own arguments (a usage error is 3 for soup eval gate) reads as a failed checkpoint, so run the command once by hand first.
soup probe sleeper2A MAJOR verdict, or a rejected input. The same holds for soup probe truth and soup probe harm.
soup probe interference2The worst pair scores 0.20 or more in absolute value, or a rejected input.

soup shrink2DON'T SHIP: perplexity regression above --tolerance.
soup shrink1Anything else that fails once the command is running: an unreadable --calib, a model that fails to load, a bad value that Click does not check. A mistyped flag or a missing required option is Click's 2, the same number as DON'T SHIP.
soup draft measure0The report was produced. Without --min-acceptance no acceptance rate fails the run.
soup draft measure2--min-acceptance was given and the measured acceptance rate is below it. Also a Click error.
soup draft measure1An error: unreadable prompts, a bad --sweep-k, a model pair that fails to load, or a target that generated no tokens.
soup reward synth0A verifier was emitted, or --plan-only printed the plan.
soup reward synth2Refused: the verifier could not tell the references from perturbed negatives. Nothing is left at -o.
soup reward synth1Usage or runtime error: no -o, an existing output without --force, an output that is not a .py file.
soup reward stress0Robust: the junk completions stayed under --max-gameable.

soup reward stress1Usage or runtime error: the target was not found or could not be loaded, a bad --attacks list.
soup recipes verify0Every config that could be checked attaches. That can mean everything was unverified, so read the report.
soup recipes verify2A config cannot attach.
soup recipes verify3A --config that is missing, unparseable or refused by the loader (Config does not parse: ..., a staged field included), or a Click error.
soup recipes verify1torch, transformers or peft is missing or fails to import, or a crash. Since v0.77.0 the --config is read first, so a missing or unparseable config exits 3 even on an install without torch (through v0.76.1 this 1 hid it).

Provenance, locks and plans

CommandCodeMeans
soup attest emit0Statement printed or written. --sign sigstore signs it with a Sigstore bundle; without the extra it does not fall back to an unsigned statement, see the 2 row.
soup attest emit2Rejected input: an invalid stage or SHA, a signing failure (ed25519 without a usable key), --sign sigstore without the [sigstore] extra, without --output, with --key, or with no ambient credential and no --interactive-oidc when the Sigstore trust root can be loaded (nothing is written; if the trust root cannot be loaded, for example offline, the run exits 1 instead), a write failure, or --attach-to-registry without --output.
soup attest emit1--attach-to-registry failed after the statement was written, or a Sigstore signing request failed at run time, which includes a trust root that cannot be loaded (for example offline) even when no credential is present either. An explicit signing request never degrades to an unsigned statement.
soup attest verify0The signature is valid: an ed25519 signature against the key embedded in the sidecar, or a Sigstore bundle against the --cert-identity and --cert-oidc-issuer you supplied. That shows the statement matches its sidecar, not who signed it: for ed25519 pass --public-key trusted.pem to require a specific signer. The subject digest is asserted by the signer and is not re-checked against an artifact.
soup attest verify3Invalid: a tampered statement or wrong key, an unsigned sidecar, no public key to verify with, an embedded key that does not match --public-key, a Sigstore sidecar with no bundle or without both --cert-identity and --cert-oidc-issuer.

soup attest verify1The Sigstore verifier is unavailable (for example its trust root cannot be fetched), which is reported as an outage and not as tampering.

Commands that start something

CommandCodeMeans
soup train0Training finished and the adapter is saved. Also --dry-run on a valid config, and --cloud without --cloud-submit (it prints a plan and starts nothing). A run stopped early by --gate or training.eval_gate with on_regression: stop, by the loss watchdog, or by a reward-hack or echo-trap halt also exits 0: soup train does not turn the stop into a failure, so check the run's output and metrics.
soup train1The config is missing, unreadable, not valid YAML, over a read limit (since v0.76.1: larger than 1 MiB, nested deeper than 100 levels or expanding past its alias allowance, each reported in one line naming the file) or invalid (an unknown key is refused, and since v0.77.0 so is a staged field set away from its default, data.remove_unused_columns: true or a quantization the task never applies: Config validation error: with one line per setting), the hardware-fit gate refuses the run (--allow-oom-attempt overrides it), a --gate suite cannot be loaded, a --replay file does not exist, a data.chat_template that is not registered or a dataset that loads zero training rows (both also under --dry-run; since v0.76.1 the second includes a preference dataset none of whose rows can be written in one layout, and since v0.77.0 a preference task whose rows lack prompt, chosen or rejected, which v0.76.1 passed under --dry-run), a --gate suite with no tasks or a repeated task name (since v0.77.0), a reward_fn: judge_rank run that could make more judge calls than training.grpo_judge_max_calls and a Sesame CSM dataset row that is not one clip with one transcript message (both since v0.77.0, checked after the data loads and before the model does, --dry-run included), --find-lr that cannot run its sweep (no report is written), --resume or --hf-resume together with relora_steps or on task: unlearn, a --diagnose-gate evidence file that cannot be read, --gpus above 1 given with --no-reexec and without --dry-run (it prints the launch command and stops), or training raised an error. The SFT trainer also refuses to save the final model, and exits 1, when the last logged loss or the trainable weights are non-finite.
soup train2A flag override that fails validation (the --replay options), an invalid tracker option, an invalid --cloud or --gpu (--cloud takes modal, lambda or, since v0.77.0, runpod), a refused cloud plan (Cloud plan failed: ..., for example a RunPod plan whose output directory already exists), or --diagnose-gate finding a MAJOR mode. The last one fires after training: the adapter is already saved and the run is recorded as finished. A mistyped flag is also 2.
soup train3--diagnose-gate finding a mode that did not run (NOT_RUN). Like the MAJOR exit it fires after training, with the adapter already saved. Also, since v0.77.0, a standard input that is a pipe or a redirected file when neither --yes nor --dry-run is given (stdin is not a TTY, so the start-training confirmation cannot be answered. Pass --yes to start without the confirmation.), after the config is read and before the data or the model loads (a config refused at load still exits 1 first): piping y into the prompt no longer answers it, so pass --yes in scripts.
soup trainthe submit call's codeWith --cloud modal, --cloud lambda or --cloud runpod plus --cloud-submit, the return code of the submit call (1 when the backend's submit is unavailable, for example RUNPOD_API_KEY or RUNPOD_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY unset). The RunPod controller has not been run against a real RunPod account yet (tracked as #2098).
soup trainthe launcher's codeWith --gpus above 1 the run is handed to accelerate launch. On Linux and macOS os.execvp replaces Soup's own process, so the code is the launcher's rather than Soup's. On Windows, since v0.76.0, Soup runs the launcher as a child process, waits for it and exits with its code; Ctrl+C waits for the launcher's own shutdown. Before v0.76.0 the Windows call returned at once with exit 0 while the launcher kept running, and the launcher's code never reached the caller. A launcher that cannot be started exits 1.
soup quickstartthe child's codeExits with the code of the soup train subprocess it starts, or 0 with --dry-run.
soup llamathe child's codeExits with the code of the llama.cpp program it runs, 2 when that program is not found on PATH, 1 when it cannot be launched.
soup serve2A refused option: a non-loopback --host without --tool-auth-token, --bank, --mole or --steer with a backend other than transformers or a path outside the working directory, --kv-cache-type fp8, any --kv-cache-type with --backend vllm, sglang or mii (Use --backend transformers.), --kv-cache-type q8_0 with no quantized-cache backend installed, --auto-quant (it is unavailable), an unknown --device, or an unusable --hub.
soup serve1Other startup failures, for example a model path that does not exist.
soup mcp serve2A refused option combination: an unknown --transport, --host, --port or --auth-token with stdio, --allow-execute with sse or http, or an invalid --auth-token.
soup mcp serve1The mcp SDK is not installed, or is too old for the transport.
soup mcp runs reconcile2--expunge-launching was not passed, and no run record changed.
soup mcp runs reconcile1A launching run whose process is still alive was refused.
soup ui2Reserved: a non-loopback host (--public or --host) without a valid auth token. The command's own options cannot reach it, because a token is generated at startup and an invalid --auth-token exits 1 first, so soup ui --host 0.0.0.0 starts the server.
soup ui1An invalid --auth-token, or the [ui] extra is not installed.
soup can run1Without --yes it prints the confirmation panel, exits 1 and runs nothing. Also an unreadable can.
soup can runthe child's codeWith --yes, the exit code of the training subprocess is passed through, then that of the deploy step when --deploy is set.
soup doctor0Advisory findings (a missing optional extra, a torchvision mismatch, a core dependency below its floor, which since v0.76.1 includes a Typer below 0.15.4 wherever soup doctor can start: below Typer 0.12.4 no command can, and 0.12.4 to 0.15.3 start only next to Click 8.1 or older) and settings your config writes that its backend never reads do not change the exit code.
soup doctor1A required core dependency is missing or incompatible, or an installed package, in an extra group included, is beyond the ceiling Soup declares for it. A missing or outdated [train] member stays advisory.
soup doctor2--config named a file that is missing, unparseable, over a YAML read limit (since v0.76.1) or fails the schema (every load refusal, an unknown key among them). It is reported after the system, GPU and dependency tables and any environment issues. Since v0.77.0 a config that cannot be loaded stops the command before All checks passed! is printed (#2106); through v0.76.1 that line could print above the refusal. Since v0.77.0 the refusals include a staged field set away from its default and a deprecated value, which v0.76 only warned about. Unknown keys are reported together, but a cross-field refusal is reported one at a time (the first it hits), so fix it and run the command again until it prints no error.

Commands with no verdict code of their own

Besides Click's exit 2 for a bad invocation, these exit only 0 or 1 (one exception since v0.77.0: soup recipes use on a recipe the catalog marks unavailable exits 3): the exit-code lines that v0.76.0 added to them are all 1, and none adds another code.

  • soup init, soup cost, soup card, soup diff, soup history, soup why, soup profile, soup sweep (1 also when every arm failed, or when a --param sets a staged field away from its default, since v0.77.0), soup autopilot, soup ci init
  • soup advise (run, explain and compare), soup recipes (other than verify; since v0.77.0 soup recipes use exits 3 for a recipe the catalog marks unavailable, kimi-k2-sft and kimi-k2-thinking-grpo, and 1 for an unknown name), soup registry (since v0.77.0 a name:tag that matches more than one entry exits 1 and lists the candidate ids; push --data and --idempotency-key refusals are 1 too)
  • soup eval benchmark (1 when nothing was measured or saved), soup eval custom, soup eval judge (1 also when the judge stops answering: three requests in a row with their retries spent end the run, print the judge URL and how many items were not judged, and the scores from before the outage are shown but not saved), soup eval auto (1 also when every leg was skipped, since v0.77.0), soup eval compare, soup eval leaderboard, soup eval human, soup eval aider
  • soup data inspect, convert, merge, dedup, filter, stats, sample, split, search, preview, from-traces, review, ingest, preprocess, generate, topics and clean. Since v0.76.0 soup data from-traces --judge against a judge that is down exits 1 and writes nothing (it used to write an empty file and exit 0), and a provider-backed soup data forge, augment or distill-prompt run in which every call failed exits 1 and writes nothing. Since v0.77.0 soup data clean, inspect and stats skip a row that is not a JSON object with a warning instead of exiting 1, and soup ingest exits 1 when --output is the --logs file or a hard link to it.
  • soup runs show, compare, replay and delete
  • soup can pack, inspect, verify, publish and fork
  • soup deploy ollama, soup deploy hf-space, soup agent synth, soup agent eval

soup eval custom never exits non-zero on a low score, so it cannot act as a checkpoint test for soup adapters bisect on its own. Several validating commands outside the tables above, among them soup export, soup merge, soup quantize, soup push, soup infer, soup fetch, soup ingest, soup tunability, soup spectrum scan, soup compile, soup data recipe, soup deploy autopilot and soup loop, use 1 or 2 for a rejected argument and have no verdict. For example soup export exits 1 for an unknown or removed --format (--format awq and gptq since v0.77.0) and 2 for a removed flag such as --bits, soup quantize --to awq or gptq exits 2, and soup loop watch --detach checks --poll-interval and --max-iterations in the parent since v0.77.0 and exits 2 without spawning a child.
